content.text:
“But how did you deduce the telegram?”
“Why, of course I knew that you had not written a letter, since I sat opposite to you all morning. I see also in your open desk there that you have a sheet of stamps and a thick bundle of postcards. What could you go into the post-office for, then, but to send a wire? Eliminate all other factors, and the one which remains must be the truth.”
“In this case it certainly is so,” I replied, after a little thought. “The thing, however, is, as you say, of the simplest.”
content.source: Arthur Conan Doyle, The Sign of the Four, chapter 1

content.text:
Along the **Walk of Stars** by the Olympic Lake, famous people have left their handprints. In each round **four of the five names really are on the walk**, but one is an impostor. Walk along it and find out **who does not belong among the stars**.

In each round you have **only one try**.

questions.explain: Elvis Presley died in 1977, long before the walk was created. All three of his Grammy awards were for gospel, though.
Freddie Mercury lived and recorded in Munich for several years in the early 1980s. But the walk was only created 12 years after his death.
